qt: to the Commission András Tivadar Kulja (PPE) Subject:

Chronic respiratory diseases are a major cause of morbidity, mortality and health inequalities across Europe, placing a significant burden on citizens, healthcare systems and the economy. Conditions such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain largely underdiagnosed or are identified at a late stage, limiting opportunities for timely intervention and effective management. Addressing this burden is crucial in order to improve citizens’ health, strengthen the EU’s prevention, resilience and competitiveness, make healthcare systems more effective and help maintain a healthy workforce. In light of the 2025 report by the World Health Organization’s Regional Office for Europe1 on chronic respiratory diseases, which recommends scaling up early detection: 1.

How does the Commission assess the burden of chronic respiratory diseases and the extent of underdiagnosis across Member States, and what comparable EU-level data does it use to monitor prevalence, diagnosis and access to timely care?

How does the Commission intend to build on existing EU initiatives, such as Healthier Together, and strengthen its support for Member States in improving early detection and management of chronic respiratory diseases?

How could the Commission further support respiratory health, including better support for chronic respiratory disease detection and management, through prevention-oriented health system reforms and EU funding instruments?
Chronic respiratory diseases in the WHO European Region, https://www.who.int/europe/publications/i/item/WHO-EURO-2025-12340-52112-79990. 1
